_comment: SmartCuff GUI update manifest. Fetched by the installed GUI over plain
public HTTPS -- there is deliberately NO credential in the client. See
README.md for why an embedded token was rejected.
This file is the ONLY thing the updater needs to read. Keep it small and
keep it valid JSON: a malformed manifest must fail soft in the client, but
there is no reason to rely on that.
The installer is a GitHub Release asset rather than a repository blob.
Keep installer_url version-specific: an existing manifest must always
resolve to the exact immutable bytes whose size and SHA-256 it declares.
notes:
Smart Cuff v3.1.375 applies the requested protocol-specific PVR peak ranges.

Smart Const accepts supported peaks from 30 to 140 mmHg and commands min(peak+5,130). Accepted peaks from 130 through 140 therefore select 130. High Max accepts 30 to 150 and commands min(peak+5,140); accepted peaks from 140 through 150 select 140. Failed quality checks and peaks outside the applicable range return 80, without adding 5. Existing SNR, shape/support and artifact checks remain required. No smart cropping or controller tuning is introduced.

High Max has a 14.5-second computation budget, reserving 0.5 seconds for result delivery; Smart Const retains 9.5 seconds plus that reserve. Live calculations measured 7.957 seconds (High Max, 185/115, 72 bpm), 7.288 seconds (High Max, 185/115, 50 bpm) and 8.873 seconds (Smart Const, 120/80, 72 bpm), all at 1 mL simulator volume with a GE Large Adult Long cuff. The first run detected 142.54 and selected 140. Physical STOP cancelled calculation and prevented refill; vented safety was reached in 4.297 seconds. No completed run needed the added 10-15-second interval, so late-interval physical STOP remains unexercised.

The mandatory ten-minute seed213 soak completed 5 cycles, with 30107/30107 telemetry frames (100.00000%). Its detailed scores are attached. Protocol completion does not establish accurate tracking on this large cuff: the first Smart Const deflation achieved 0.59 of the commanded rate. This uses actual phase events; the harness's 0.55 value included the subsequent calculation pause. Controller gains, calibration and safety thresholds are preserved.

Known transport limitation: the separate 50 bpm High Max trial completed but failed its transport gate after one hold frame was malformed in raw serial bytes (8539/8540, 99.9883%). The checksum rejected it. This failure remains in POLICY_VALIDATION.json; clean transport qualification is false, and this release does not fix the previously recorded link corruption. One earlier setting change was blocked before a trial because ProSim still measured residual pressure above 5 mmHg; the retry used a vented pause and the same guard.

Validation: firmware compile passed; seven standard GUI scripts, built-in protocol parity, and 139 focused tests passed (one Git-only check skipped in the isolated source snapshot). All 15 native single-file cases passed in MATLAB R2026a Update 5 and Octave 11.3. The single-file firmware MEX matched 85 independent host-core executions with zero decision/reason differences and maximum peak difference below 0.000005 mmHg. These synthetic and reused bench tests are not independent clinical validation or evidence that peak+5 maximizes constant-hold amplitude.

The firmware, GUI report validation, MATLAB entries, HTML help and three-page PDF are aligned. Firmware: rev27v-followup-350, dated 11/11/2026. Default source: 3f13554733df48f5389458f19256a2f83ed4d3dc. Installer: 224471953 bytes; SHA-256 4366c058c81ac46e507939977ff8f33ca08fd2da2711faa9052e87ec41c67d4a. Build UTC: 2026-11-11T16:10:05.9938384Z. Authenticode is unsigned as previously authorized; first installations may require More info -> Run anyway in SmartScreen. Automatic updates retain the existing verified-download, idle/pump-off/vented and calibration-preserving upload gates.
_channel_note: stable is the only channel today. If a test channel is ever added, publish
a second manifest (version-beta.json) rather than adding branching logic to
the client -- the client stays a dumb fetch-and-compare.
